lessons.title: The mapping table you put in the migration pack
lessons.why: Names from the old platform are not Connect resources. Write the map before you build the queues.
paras: A CUCM calling search space is not a routing profile, but the profile is the closest idea of 'who can receive what'. A partition is not a Connect object. A UCCX CSQ and a UCCE skill group map to a queue. Precision steps map to routing criteria. A script, an Architect flow, and an Avaya vector map to a contact flow.
Finesse maps to the CCP or a Streams desktop. CUIC maps to real-time metrics, historical metrics, and the CTR. A recording trunk maps to the recording block and S3.
points: Write one row per old object, with the Connect object and the pitfall.
Skills can become proficiencies or extra queues. Pick one and say why.
Hunt pilots become queues plus priority and delay.
The lab translator does this row by row.
lessons.mistake: Creating a queue named after every CUCM partition.

lessons.title: A migration playbook
lessons.why: The order is identity, network, flows, a pilot number, reports, then the port.
paras: Federate a pilot team and prove the CCP on their real network. Rebuild the busiest script as a flow with error branches and a module for recording. Staff one queue. Compare a day of contacts with CUIC or the old wallboard, using written formulas.
Then port a pilot number with a rollback date. Only after audio, pop, and WFM look right do you move the range. Global Resiliency comes after the instance is the system of record, not before.
points: Translate quick connects from the old speed-dial list, and delete the dead ones.
Hours and holidays are a data migration, not a memory test.
Keep a glossary so 'skill' means one thing in the new design.

lessons.title: Pitfalls that show up in every platform
lessons.why: The platforms differ. The mistakes repeat.
paras: People map skills to queues and also to proficiencies and double-route. They forget that a PSTN transfer drops attributes, so the CUCM agent has no screen pop. They compare AHT that includes ACW with AHT that does not. They port the number before UDP 3478 is open. They discover campaign or outbound country limits on week one.
Webex Contact Center is a competing CCaaS, not a card you slot into Connect. Genesys Edges and Avaya port networks do not become Connect constructs. You replace them or you transfer to them.
points: Write the AHT formula on the report.
Test the external transfer with a real desk phone.

lessons.title: CUIC and the Connect report are different clocks
lessons.why: If you do not write both formulas, the business will say the new platform is slower or faster than it is.
paras: CUIC intervals, Genesys historical, and Avaya CMS all define handle time, abandon, and service level with small differences. Connect's queue duration and ACW are visible on the CTR. Build one table: old metric, new metric, included or excluded, source field.
Real-time boards will not match during dual-run because agents are split. Compare a pilot queue with itself, not the whole old center with the new pilot.
points: Service level target seconds must match or you publish two truths.
Transfers inflate contact counts. Deduplicate on the chain.
Outbound and inbound should not share one AHT.
The data lake is where you freeze the definition.
lessons.mistake: A red dashboard in week one that is only a formula change.
